prompt: Hypothetical. Capital Rs 50,000. Risk per trade 2%. How many rupees is the risk per trade?
solution: Risk per trade = 50,000 x 2% = 50,000 x 0.02 = Rs 1,000. At the 2% level, the risk check passes.

prompt: Hypothetical. Capital Rs 50,000. Risk per trade 1.5%. How many rupees is the risk per trade?
solution: Risk per trade = 50,000 x 1.5% = 50,000 x 0.015 = Rs 750. This is below 2%, so the risk check passes.

prompt: Your form shows 6% risk per trade. You think it is fine, because 6% sounds small. Which response matches this gate?

options.text: Fail with the hard note, because above 5% is the hard level.
Fail with a note only, which is the same as a pass.

explanations.a: The gate does not use a 10% level. Above 5% fails with the hard note.
explanations.c: Above 5% is a hard fail, not a pass with a note.
explanations.d: A fail with a note is still a fail. It is not the same as a pass.

prompt: Spot the mistake: "Passing G7 means I am ready to make money with my capital." Which part of this statement is wrong?

options.text: "Passing G7". This is only a statement about the gate, and it is correct.
"means I am ready to make money". This is wrong. The gate does not say you are ready to profit.
"with my capital". This is correct wording for the plan.

explanations.a: This part is correct. Passing G7 is a real result of the gate, not a claim about profit.
explanations.c: This part is correct. The plan covers your capital, so the words fit the form.

prompt: What does the printed one-page plan show?

options.text: A second copy of the plan, saved as a separate file.
A view of the saved plan, with every field shown.
A new plan that is written each time you print.
Only the risk per trade field.

explanations.a: The printed plan is not a second copy. It is a view of the saved plan.
explanations.c: Printing does not write a new plan. It shows the saved one.
explanations.d: The printed plan shows every field, not only the risk field.

prompt: What happens when you edit the form after a save?

options.text: Each save has a date and older versions stay in your history.
The edit is lost when you close the page.
All the gates reset to zero.

explanations.a: Older versions are kept in your history. Nothing is deleted when you edit.
explanations.c: Each save is kept with its date, so the edit is not lost.
explanations.d: Editing the form does not reset the gates. The gate results are read from their own records.
